svg.text: K5b HANDLER — 5 axes, one tang for everything
X in a dry rail box, a hanging mast, Z, a Y arm, a roll wrist and a pin jaw. It carries, tips, pours, flips and weighs.
X 1 400 mm 1 m/s · Z 900 mm · Y 380 mm
roll about Y: 0–200 rpm, 12 Nm · jaw 20–300 N
load pins in the jaw: ±5 g dosing by loss in weight
tang 6 × 32 × 60 with two Ø 8 holes on every item
dry rail box: X belt, 1 400 mm

g.text: Y arm, 3° slope to the mast

svg.text: X runs into the page; roll is about Y
The common tang and the pin jaw
Two pins enter the two holes (form fit). Load pins
in the jaw weigh whatever hangs from the tang.
Dose by tipping, stop by weight
The jaw holds the box flange and rolls it with a ±2°
dither at 8 Hz; it stops when the target weight is out.
Breaded Schnitzel: fried on a rack, turned as a rack pair
The cutlet is never gripped. A second rack is laid on top, tangs back to back; the pair is lifted, drained,
rolled 180° about its own centre over the pan and lowered: 200 mL fat in a 28 cm pan = 3.8 mm deep.

g.text: 1/4 Fry: the rack holds two crumbed cutlets in the fat; the handler rocks it ±10 mm so fat washes over the edges
2/4 Pair: a second rack is laid on top, tangs back to back in the jaw; the pair is lifted clear of the pan and drained
3/4 Turn: the wrist rolls the pair 180° about its own centre while X and Z keep that centre still over the pan
4/4 Lower and fry the second side; dosing (top right) uses the same roll axis and the load pins in the jaw
